events.text:
**Recommendation: Grand Haven, or Muskegon if it's calm.** I expect all four ports to be slow to average this week. The newest reports are 6 days old (2025-09-10), and I couldn't get live conditions. The tool only returned last week's buoy averages. I have no wind forecast and no cold-layer depths, so check the marine forecast before you go.

| Port | My rating (0–4) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 2 (average) | Best recent boat history, but the newest report has no boat details. |
| Muskegon | 2 (average) | The only port with a boat report on 9/10, and it was positive. |
| South Haven | 1 (below average) | Slow on 9/10, and no boat-specific report. |
| St. Joseph | 1 (below average) | Slow boat reports for three weeks, and the piers were hard to reach. |

**What the reports say**
- **Muskegon:**
  - On 9/10, boats that could get out found a mix of immature and mature salmon in 150–220 ft of water, 70–150 ft down. Green or white flies worked best. Catch quality wasn't rated. (Muskegon, 2025-09-10)
  - The phrase "when boats were able to get out" suggests wind or waves limited trips. (Muskegon, 2025-09-10)
  - A week earlier, salmon were scattered. The best fishing was 70–120 ft down in 80–160 ft of water, on flasher-flies and glow spoons, rated 1. (Muskegon, 2025-09-03)
- **Grand Haven:**
  - The 9/10 report only covered the pier, which was slow (rated 1). (Grand Haven, 2025-09-10)
  - On 9/3 the boat bite was rated 0 because of warmer water. Fish were 70–120 ft down in 80–150 ft of water. Glow spoons and green or white flies worked best. (Grand Haven, 2025-09-03)
  - Before that, boat fishing was rated 3 on 8/20 and 8/13, with fish 50–110 ft down in 80–220 ft of water. (Grand Haven, 2025-08-20; Grand Haven, 2025-08-13)
- **South Haven:**
  - Overall fishing was slow (rated 1), with a few kings and steelhead. Most fish came from casting spoons. (South Haven, 2025-09-10)
  - Boat fishing was rated 2 on 8/27, with fish taken from 35 ft out to well past 120 ft. (South Haven, 2025-08-27)
- **St. Joseph:**
  - On 9/10, "the few boats that did make it out experienced tough fishing" (rated 0). Anglers also had trouble reaching the piers. This report isn't salmon-specific. (St. Joseph, 2025-09-10)
  - On 9/3, boat fishing was rated 1. A couple of good catches came around 120 ft, and some boats fished 35 ft north and south of the piers. (St. Joseph, 2025-09-03)
  - The last salmon-specific boat report was rated 2 (70 ft, spoons). (St. Joseph, 2025-08-27)
  - Salmon are showing up in the rivers, but only a few. Black River had a few salmon for shore and boat anglers (rated 1) on 9/10. St. Joseph River had some Chinook in the lower river and at Berrien Springs dam (rated 1) on 9/10.
- **Water temperature:** Last week's buoy averages were about 68–69°F at all four ports, with little change over the week. The surface was 60–65°F during the early-August and late-August upwelling weeks, when fishing was better.

**History (same time of year, earlier seasons)**
- Mid-to-late September boat fishing at Grand Haven and Muskegon was usually in deep water. Fish were typically 40–140 ft down in 100–220 ft of water, mostly immature Chinook and steelhead. Spoons and flies worked.
  - Grand Haven was rated 3 on 2024-09-18 and 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-21.
  - Muskegon was rated 1–3 in those weeks.
- South Haven and St. Joseph were usually 0–2 in the same weeks, and anglers were often fishing deep (120+ ft).
- Upwelling weeks brought a short burst of excellent fishing near the pierheads. Grand Haven was rated 4 on 2023-09-13 with a 10°F surface drop.
- Pier and river fishing at St. Joseph was good in some past mid-Septembers (2024-09-11) when the water dropped.

**My read**
- I'd expect Grand Haven and Muskegon to fish about average in 100–220 ft of water. Run flies or flasher-flies and spoons 60–120 ft down, following the 9/10 Muskegon report.
- If a north or east wind drops the surface temperature, I'd expect fish to move toward the pierheads and Grand Haven to jump to good. The reference guidance (Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension) says upwelling pushes salmon toward shore. Nothing in this week's data shows an upwelling yet.
- I'd expect South Haven and St. Joseph to stay slow for boats. Both are the weakest in the recent reports and in past seasons. If you fish there, I'd go deep (110–120+ ft) and troll spoons.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon share one buoy, so their water readings can't separate them. Ranking Grand Haven first is a judgment call based on its stronger August results and past Septembers.

**Caveats**
- Reports are weekly, and fall conditions change fast.
- The Grand Haven boat bite was rated 0 on 9/3 and 9/10 had no boat report, so the average rating there rests on older data.
- Several ports mentioned boats being unable to get out. Check the wind and wave forecast first, and stay in port if it's rough.
